hermite_related.title: The exact spectrum of the finite free convolution coupling matrix E_n: both numerical conjectures of arXiv:2604.11922 proved for every degree
hermite_related.description: **Source.** Baran Hashemi, *Spectral Structure in Finite Free Information Inequalities and `p`-Stam Phase Transitions*, [arXiv:2604.11922](https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.11922) v2 (math.PR; cs.LG, math.CO cross-lists; v1 13 Apr 2026, v2 15 May 2026 — v1 carried the different title *FlowBoost Reveals Phase Transitions and Spectral Structure in Finite Free Information Inequalities*, so quote v2). Background: Jorge Garza-Vargas, Nikhil Srivastava, Zachary Stier, *Finite Free Information Inequalities*, arXiv:2602.15822 v1 (the source's `[GVS26]`).

statements.label: Symmetry of the finite free convolution coupling matrix: for every degree n = N+1 and every injective enumeration u of the roots of He_n, the matrix E_n defined by implicit differentiation of the convolution root map at the Hermite diagonal satisfies E_n^T = E_n
The eigenvalues of E_n: charpoly(E_n) = prod_{k=0}^{n-1} (X - 2^{-k/2}), for every degree, independent of n

The source's Conjecture (Geometric spectrum of E_n): the singular values of E_n are exactly 2^{-k/2}, k = 0..n-1, stated as charpoly(E_n^T E_n) = prod_{k=0}^{n-1} (X - 2^{-k}) -- a rational characteristic polynomial
E_n is doubly stochastic in the sense E_n 1 = 1 and 1^T E_n = 1^T (columns and rows sum to 1), obtained here as the m = N case of the eigen-relation rather than from the Gauss-Lucas coupling argument
Unconditional trace identity: trace(E_n) - 1 = sum_{k=1}^{n-1} 2^{-k/2}, i.e. the source's Tr(E_n|_W) formula, which it derives only under both of its conjectures
Non-vacuity of the hypotheses: He 2 = X^2 - 1 and He 3 = X^3 - 3X, so ![-1,1] and ![-sqrt 3, 0, sqrt 3] are injective enumerations of their roots and every headline theorem has instances
Anchor at n = 2: Emat 1 ![-1,1] sqrt 2 = !![(2+sqrt 2)/4, (2-sqrt 2)/4; (2-sqrt 2)/4, (2+sqrt 2)/4], with charpoly (X-1)(X-1/sqrt 2) recomputed independently from Matrix.charpoly_fin_two

Negative controls: the spectrum is not {2^{-k/2} : k = 1..n} (the eigenvalue 1 is present), it is not {1} with multiplicity n, and injectivity of the node vector is load-bearing -- for u = ![-1,-1], which satisfies hroot, E_2 is the constant matrix and its charpoly is not the dyadic product
Christoffel-Darboux for the probabilists' Hermite polynomials: (X - y) * sum_{m<=n} He_m(y)/m! * He_m * n! = He_{n+1} He_n(y) - He_n He_{n+1}(y)

The bridge from the source's coefficient formula to the operator: e^{-D^2/2} x^m = He_m, and for every p of degree <= n the source's (eq:boxplus_coeff) applied to (p, He_n) returns e^{-D^2/2} p, i.e. p (+)_n He_n = e^{-D^2/2} p

The eigen-relation behind the dyadic law: e^{-D^2/2} He_m = He_m(.;2) (the variance-2 Appell-Hermite) and He_m(c x; 2) = c^m He_m(x) whenever c^2 = 2 -- so He_m is an eigenvector of 'convolve with He_n, then rescale by sqrt 2' with eigenvalue 2^{m/2}

hermite_related.paper_title: The coupling matrix of the finite free convolution\\ at the Hermite diagonal is symmetric,\\ and its spectrum is exactly $\{2^{-k/2}\}$
hermite_related.paper_abstract: The finite free additive convolution $\bx_n$ of Marcus, Spielman and Srivastava acts on the root vectors of monic real-rooted polynomials of degree $n$ by a map $\Omega$ that is smooth at a simple-root configuration.  Hashemi's \emph{coupling matrix} $E_n$ is the partial Jacobian $\partial\Omega(\cdot,h)/\partial\alpha$ frozen at the Hermite diagonal $\alpha=\beta=h$, where $h$ is the root vector of the degree-$n$ probabilists' Hermite polynomial $\He_n$.  On numerical evidence --- the ten leading singular values at nine degrees between $10$ and $90$, and a relative Frobenius asymmetry below $10^{-10}$ --- he conjectures that $E_n$ is symmetric and that its singular values on $\one^\perp$ are exactly $\{2^{-k/2}:k=1,\dots,n-1\}$, the same numbers at every degree.  We prove both, at every degree and in exact form: $E_n^{\!\top}=E_n$; the characteristic polynomial of $E_n$ is $\prod_{k=0}^{n-1}(X-2^{-k/2})$; that of the Gram matrix $E_n^{\!\top}E_n$ is $\prod_{k=0}^{n-1}(X-2^{-k})$; and $\tr E_n-1=\sum_{k=1}^{n-1}2^{-k/2}$, an identity the source derives only under \emph{both} of its conjectures.  The mechanism is that convolving with $\He_n$ is the heat operator $\Gop=e^{-D^2/2}$: Christoffel--Darboux expands $\He_n/(x-u_j)$ in the Hermite basis, $\Gop\He_m$ is the variance-two Hermite polynomial and $\Hetwo_m(\sqrt2\,x)=2^{m/2}\He_m(x)$, so $E_n$ is the matrix of a rescaled heat operator --- manifestly symmetric in one basis, diagonal in another. Nothing here is an exhaustive computation: every statement holds at every degree at once, and the source's numerics are reproduced only as a check that the algebraic definition used here is the analytic object it is meant to be.  The three corollaries the source states under ``Assume Conjecture~4.1'' --- the full singular value decomposition of the convolution Jacobian, the local stability constant, and the finite free central limit rate $\lambda_{\mathrm{CLT}}=1/\sqrt2$ uniform in $n$ --- therefore hold unconditionally. Every lemma, proposition and theorem below is machine-checked in Lean~4; the two corollaries and the two remarks are not, and say so.

hermite_related.title: The exact worst-case upper tail under a bounded fourth moment: sharp values and exact dual certificates for the fifteen cells arXiv:2607.05226 could not certify
hermite_related.description: For a real random variable `X` with `E X = 0`, `E X² = 1` and `E X⁴ ≤ κ`, how large can `P(X ≥ t)` be? Two classes are studied here, both formalised over honest probability measures on `ℝ` (Bochner integrals, with integrability of `x⁴` part of the definition — without it `∫ x⁴ ∂μ` silently returns `0` for a heavy-tailed law and the moment constraint would be vacuous):

statements.label: Weak duality for the four-moment upper-tail problem over probability measures on R, with integrability of x^4 in the definition of the class
Zelen's branch (t^2 - g*t - 1 > 0) is sharp for the class with fourth moment only BOUNDED, with an exact perfect-square dual certificate q = (u/u(t))^2
The ten rational cells among the thirteen skewness-pinned instances arXiv:2607.05226 reports as uncertified: 4/9, 4/45, 3/7, 3/391, 7/15, 19/159, 16/77, 1/74, 7/51, 4/65
The source paper's own pinned-versus-free cross-check at (t,kappa) = (2,3), exact: 2/19 with E X^3 = 0 pinned, and 2/11 refuted in the pinned class
The central branch (t^2 - g*t - 1 < 0) is sharp, with the Hermite quartic certificate; nonnegativity of that certificate is automatic whenever r1 < t < r2
The three skewness-pinned cells below Zelen's branch: (10-sqrt 14)/14, (5-sqrt 5)/10, (4761-307*sqrt 69)/7314

The source paper's algebraic system (S) for Regime IIIb collapses to the single relation 2c(c-b) = (b+t)^2, and its assertion that any solution yields V1 exactly is then proved by weak duality plus attainment
An exact rational point of Regime IIIb: at (t,kappa) = (3/10, 2151/400) the maximum is 1025/1176, and all three closed forms of the source paper's map are refuted there

The source paper's single `fail` cell (t,kappa) = (1/2,3/2): the maximum is the value the collapsed system takes at the root of 16b^6+208b^5+768b^4+476b^3-849b^2-508b+316 in (0.8028,0.8029), sandwiched strictly between the Regime IIIa plateau value 2/3 and 0.6674
Negative controls at a solved cell: 1/2 too large, 2/5 too small, and the class non-empty
Zelen's branch hypothesis is not decoration: one cell outside it has zelenValue = 3/7, and 3/7 is provably not the maximum there
The bound(eps) cell (t,kappa) = (1/2,2) upgraded to an exact certificate; the sandwich (0.7262, 0.7263) confirms the sextic value the source paper publishes
The bound(eps) cell (t,kappa) = (1/2,3) upgraded to an exact certificate: the root of 16b^6+208b^5+768b^4+284b^3-2097b^2-1132b+1756 in (1.1900614,1.1900615), sandwiched in (0.7896, 0.7897)

The three-moment cell arXiv:2607.05226 reports as `fail` without ever naming it, identified from its artifact repository and solved exactly: for X >= 0 with E X = 1, E X^2 = 2, E X^3 = 9/2, max P(X >= 5) = 1/95

Machine-checked erratum: Lemma 2.2 of arXiv:2312.04925 (Kwan-Wigderson), attributed to Zelen 1954 eq. (12), is false as printed for a != 0; refuted at E[Y^4] = 2, a = 1/2, together with the sharp value there

The solution variety of the collapsed system (S) of Regime IIIb is a rational surface: the explicit two-parameter polynomial parameterisation t = r(m^2+2m-2), b = r(2-m^2), c = 2r, proved onto, with the exact maximum at every point of an explicit region

An exact rational curve inside Regime IIIb: for 9 <= 425t^2 and 25t^2 <= 3, max P(X >= t) at kurtosis budget (2125t^4+1422t^2)/27 is exactly (375t^2-3)/(392t^2); the rational locus of IIIb is infinite and is not confined to one curve

Controls for the rational surface: Cantelli's bound for the whole class with its square certificate; the 25t^2 <= 3 window is load-bearing; all three closed forms of the source's map refuted at EVERY point of the curve, with the contact structure

The source's unproven global-solvability clause for Regime IIIb, proved on an explicit two-dimensional region: for t in [1/5,3/10] and every kappa between the two endpoint budgets, (S) has a solution with threshold t and budget kappa, and the supremum is attained

hermite_related.title: Fortuna's conjecture: is the solution of X A + A^T X = -Q entrywise nonnegative for every Hurwitz companion A? -- the n = 5 complex-pair cell that arXiv:2606.16492 leaves open
hermite_related.description: Founded 2026-09-07 from arXiv:2606.16492v1 (A. Ferrante, *On the Lyapunov equation with the state matrix in companion form*, eess.SY / math.RA). Record: `journal/2026-09-07-lyapcomp-fortuna-founding.md`.
hermite_related.paper_title: Fortuna's conjecture on the companion Lyapunov equation\\ at the first open cell: an exact verification at a degree-five\\ companion matrix with a complex-conjugate pair
hermite_related.paper_abstract: Let $a(s)=s^n+a_{n-1}s^{n-1}+\dots+a_0$ be a Hurwitz polynomial, $A$ its companion matrix and $X$ the solution of the Lyapunov equation $XA+A\tp X=-Q$ with $Q=Q\tp\psd$.  Fortuna's conjecture, as stated by Ferrante (arXiv:2606.16492), asserts that $X$ is entrywise nonnegative.  Ferrante proves it when $A$ has only real eigenvalues, records that the cases $n\le4$ can be settled by brute force and that the diagonal and the two corner entries are always nonnegative, and names the removal of the real-root assumption as the main open question.  We give an exact verification in a cell outside those bounds: at the companion matrix of $(s+1)^3(s^2+s+1)=s^5+4s^4+7s^3+7s^2+4s+1$, whose spectrum contains $\exp(\pm2\pi i/3)$ and which is not diagonalizable, the solution for every rank-one $Q=qq\tp$ is entrywise nonnegative, each of its fifteen distinct entries being written as an explicit sum of squares in $q$ with rational coefficients; the solution is also shown to be unique among symmetric matrices by an explicit inversion of the Lyapunov operator over $\Q$.  Two identities valid for every degree and every spectrum are recorded: $2a_0X_{1,n}=Q_{11}$, which turns Ferrante's corner remark into a value, and $X_{k,k-1}=a_{k-1}X_{k,n}-Q_{kk}/2$.  Controls show that the companion form and the Hurwitz hypothesis are both needed and that the conclusion is strictly stronger than $X\psd$.  Recomputing Ferrante's counterexample to total nonnegativity exactly over $\Q$, we find that the minor he names, the leading $2\times2$ principal minor, is positive ($+4355916893/28812000$), as it must be when $X\psd$, and that the negative minor is the non-principal one on rows $\{1,2\}$ and columns $\{2,3\}$, equal to $-51562093/72030$.  Outside the formal development we report a floating-point-free search ($57{,}678$ rational instances at $n=5$, no counterexample), a symbolic verification along the one-parameter family $(s+1)^3(s^2+ps+1)$, $p>0$, and the identification, for $n\le5$, of the inverse of the matrix of the quadratic form $X_{nn}$ with the Hermite matrix of $a$, whose $(n,n)$ entry is $2a_{n-1}$; this yields $X_{n,n-1}\ge0$ for every Hurwitz $a$ of degree at most $5$.  Every pinned statement is verified in Lean~4 against \emph{Mathlib} without compiled evaluation.

hermite_related.title: Rational and corner-vector designs: the 37-point antipodal 5-design for the Chebyshev and Hermite measures, the 3-adic denominator obstruction, and the two-orbit 9-design exclusion on S^3

hermite_related.paper_title: An antipodal rational $5$-design with $37$ points, a $3$-adic obstruction for the degree-five Hilbert--Kamke equations, and the nonexistence of two-orbit weighted $9$-designs on $\Sph^3$
hermite_related.paper_abstract: A Chebyshev-type quadrature of degree $m$, or an $m$-design, for a probability measure $w(t)\,dt$ on an interval $I$ is a set of distinct points of $I$ over which the unweighted average of every polynomial of degree at most $m$ equals its integral.  For the Chebyshev measure $(1-t^2)^{-1/2}dt/\pi$ on $(-1,1)$, Mishima, Lu, Sawa and Uchida determined the spectrum of antipodal rational $5$-designs with an even number of points completely, proved that none with an odd number $2N+1\le 33$ of points exists, exhibited one with $35$ points, and asked for one with $37$ points as the smallest open case.  We answer that question: the $37$ rational numbers $\{0\}\cup\{\pm m/144\}$, where $m$ runs over $\{3,11,18,25,39,81,91,99,111,117,122,123,125,127,133,137,141,143\}$, form an antipodal $5$-design.  We also record a congruence obstruction on the denominators of such designs which the purely $2$-adic machinery of the source does not see, and which together with that machinery cut the search space by a factor of about $3\cdot10^4$: writing the degree-five system in the homogeneous form $\sum m_i^2=c_2h^2$, $\sum m_i^4=c_4h^4$, the identity $x^4=x^2$ on $\ZZ/3\ZZ$ forces $3\mid h$ whenever $3\nmid c_4-c_2$, and then a mod~$9$ count forces the number of $m_i$ prime to $3$ to be divisible by $9$.  For the $37$-point system this says that every common denominator of the points is divisible by $12$, and that over the least one, $9$ or $18$ of the $18$ positive numerators are prime to~$3$; the new configuration satisfies both, at the smaller of the two allowed counts.  A second, independent part of the paper settles a question about weighted spherical designs raised by Tanino, Tamaru, Hirao and Sawa.  They construct designs on $\Sph^{n-1}$ as unions of hyperoctahedral orbits of \emph{generalized corner vectors} $v_{a,s}$, and report for $n=4$ that they could find no $11$-design, and not even a $9$-design, with two proper orbits.  We show that none exists: for every pair of orbit types $s_1,s_2\in\{0,1,2,3\}$, all $a_1,a_2>0$ and all positive weights, the four $B_4$-invariant harmonic conditions of degree at most $9$ are inconsistent.  Their own Theorem~5.7 already excludes three of the five cases of their classification, for every $n\ge3$; the content that is new here is the two remaining cases at $n=4$.  The degree is sharp --- the corresponding two-orbit $7$-design system is solvable --- and Schur's four-orbit $11$-design satisfies the very same four equations, so ``two orbits'' cannot be raised to ``four''.  Two errata in the printed formulas of that source are recorded along the way.  Every theorem and proposition below is formally verified in Lean~4, and we state precisely what lies outside that guarantee.
